newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Sentiment bears down on naphtha.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Sentiment bears down on naphtha.

text.p: Naphtha extended its losses on Monday amid softer sentiment and crude and partially in correction to last week's hike, traders said.
Naphtha April swaps fell 15 cents per barrel from Friday to $23.50/$24.80.
"There is still healthy demand," said one western trader. "But it (the price) was overdone last week."
He said prices in Asia were supported, opening the East-West arbitrage, but saw the window closing in around a month's time as "buying on the West is very strong."

IOC's last HAN cargo from Madras which lifted January 5-7 was awarded at a $16.65 per tonne discount, while its last HAN cargo from Cochin which lifted March 1-3 was awarded at a $16.50 per tonne discount.

A U.S. major and a Swiss trader emerged as sellers of first half April gasoline barrels but did not aggressively offer down cargoes with 92-octane at $28.00 per barrel fob Singapore and 95-octane at $28.65, respectively. On Friday, 92-octane was traded at $27.90 and $28.10.
But no trade was reported with the 95-octane bid only at $28.25.
But some bears in the market said April demand had slackened, and together with talk of uncommitted cargoes from the west arriving in May, saw prices under pressure.
Reflective of the weaker market, state-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) awarded its two naphtha sell tenders at lower prices than its previous awards, industry sources said.

Dutch trader Vitol won both 27,000 tonnes of high aromatic naphtha (HAN) lifting March 27-29 from Madras on the east coast at a $22.28 per tonne discount to Japanese spot quotes, fob, and 30,000 tonnes of HAN lifting April 1-3 from Cochin on the west coast at a $19.08 discount fob.
